what: A/B of the ComfyUI node's host paths: input preparation (per-frame Pillow x4 bicubic, now pooled + fused conversions) and the [-1,1] -> [0,1] output conversion (now in place).
method: identical input tensor torch.rand(81, 512, 960, 3) (target_h=2048); arm 'serial' is the pre-change implementation, arm 'pooled' is HEAD. sha256 over the returned bf16 LQ bytes proves bit-identity. min of 2 timed runs per arm; container 48-core CPU, torch 2.14.0+cpu.
environment: container, CPU-only (Pillow resize + tensor conversion); workers = min(8, cpu_count, frames)

output_conversion.what: execute(): [-1,1] -> [0,1] canvas conversion on a 1.01 GiB fp32 canvas (3x25x1408x2560)

scope: Applies to the ComfyUI node's host paths only. comfyui/bench_tiled.py times render_tiled alone (make_lq runs outside its timer), so benchmarks/tiled_render.json and every ratio in the README are unaffected — this change makes the node end-to-end faster by the prep delta, which that JSON does not measure.

pod_run.why: measured through the same code path as comfyui/bench_tiled.py (official init_pipeline + the node's _image_batch_to_lq + flashvsr_sm89_ops.render_tiled) on a real clip, so the numbers sit next to tiled_render.json's render-only times
pod_run.hardware: RTX 4090 24 GB (container), 85-frame clip, ops pack on (fp8_linears=300, lcsa=bsa)

2k.untiled_arm: skipped: the untiled 2K render does not fit a 24 GB card

pod_run.note: render_tiled is untouched, so tiled_render.json's numbers and every ratio in the README stay valid; the gain shows up as node end-to-end time.
